feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Peru's northern coast set an October heat record as the sea ran up to 9 °C above normal
entry.summary: Huanchaco near Trujillo, Peru, reached 27.8 °C, its highest October reading since 1948, and Chiclayo reached 31.8 °C. — Sources: El Popular (Trujillo), 29 October 2026, citing Imarpe and Senamhi

entry.title: Australia's weather bureau recorded a record weekly El Niño reading and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole
entry.summary: The Australian Bureau of Meteorology's weekly relative Niño3.4 index reached +2.88 °C for the week ending 25 October, the highest since its weekly series began in 2008. — Sources: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Climate Driver Update, 27 October 2026

entry.title: Correction: England's drought eased this week, and the 61 percent rainfall figure dates from 2025
entry.summary: The 61 percent rainfall figure and March target published here on 30 October come from a 31 October 2025 release. — Sources: Environment Agency, Dry weather and drought in England, 23 to 29 October 2026, published 30 October 2026 · GOV.UK, Drought likely to continue into 2026 due to record dry weather, 31 October 2025

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany, fell to 34 centimetres after its October recovery peaked
entry.summary: Germany's federal gauge network measured the Rhine at Kaub at 34 centimetres at 6am on 31 October, down from a peak of 61 centimetres on the evening of 28 October and 59 centimetres on the morning of 29 October. — Sources: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung, Pegelonline gauge network, readings 24 to 31 October 2026

entry.title: South Africa's heat warnings moved to the Eastern Cape, with extreme fire danger in the Northern Cape
entry.summary: South Africa's weather service issued heatwave advisories for Inxuba Yethemba, Chris Hani and Alfred Nzo in the Eastern Cape, running to 1 November, and warned of extremely high fire danger across most of the Northern Cape. — Sources: South African Weather Service warnings via The Citizen, 29 October 2026, and IOL, 30 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore's haze stayed in the moderate band every hour for six days from 26 October
entry.summary: Singapore's 24-hour PSI has been 100 or below in all five regions every hour since midnight on 26 October, and read 57 to 72 at 1pm on 31 October. — Sources: National Environment Agency, Singapore, hourly 24-hour PSI data, 24 to 31 October 2026

entry.title: Sarawak, Malaysia's haze peaked on 25 October and closed 27 schools in Tebedu
entry.summary: Serian in Sarawak, Malaysia, reached an air pollutant index of 194 on 25 October, near the very unhealthy band, and 27 schools in Tebedu closed for the next day. — Sources: Free Malaysia Today, 25 October 2026 · Kosmo, 25 October 2026 · The Star, 27 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire hotspots rose again on 29 October despite rain arriving in Kalimantan
entry.summary: Indonesia's forestry ministry counted 154 high-confidence fire hotspots on 29 October, up from 93 on 26 October, led by Central Kalimantan. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry via Koran Jakarta, 27 October 2026, and Okezone, 30 October 2026 · BMKG via Kompas, 26 October 2026

entry.title: The Lancet Countdown found climate change behind 68 percent of the world's heat deaths, 2016 to 2023
entry.summary: The Lancet Countdown's 2026 report puts heat-related deaths at an average of 540,800 a year between 2016 and 2023, of which 68 percent are attributed to climate change. 2023 alone had 710,000. — Sources: Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, 2026 global report, The Lancet, 27 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia counted 333,470 haze-related respiratory infections, 75,172 in children under five
entry.summary: Indonesia's health ministry recorded 333,470 acute respiratory infections in fire-hit areas between 18 August and 21 October, across 68 regencies in seven provinces, at about 3,900 new cases a day. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Health via Kontan, October 2026

entry.title: UK mortality surveillance found no excess deaths in any nation through early October
entry.summary: The UK Health Security Agency's week 44 report, published 29 October, found no deaths above baseline in England, Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland through the week ending 4 October. — Sources: UK Health Security Agency, weekly all-cause mortality surveillance, week 44 report, 29 October 2026

entry.title: The Philippines' national heat-index rules for workers took effect, with suspension at 52 °C
entry.summary: Labor Advisory No. 20, signed 27 October, sets four heat-index tiers for all employers in the Philippines, from water and shade at 27 °C to work suspension at 52 °C. — Sources: Philippines Department of Labor and Employment, Labor Advisory No. 20, Series of 2026, via BusinessMirror, 28 October 2026, and Daily Tribune, 27 October 2026 · Philippine Information Agency, Labor Advisory No. 19, October 2026

entry.title: Lagos State, Nigeria, warned employers to protect outdoor and construction workers from extreme heat
entry.summary: Lagos State's environment commissioner warned on 30 October of extreme heat linked to El Niño and the dry season, and told employers to give outdoor and construction workers and street traders shade, water and ventilation. — Sources: Vanguard, 30 October 2026

entry.title: Heat cost 573 billion potential work hours worldwide in 2025, 29 percent of them in construction
entry.summary: The Lancet Countdown's 2026 report finds heat cost 573 billion potential work hours in 2025. — Sources: Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, 2026 global report, The Lancet, 27 October 2026
